title: Certificate Utility Invoked With Transfer Or Decoding Options
detection_hypothesis: If the certificate utility is repurposed for transfer or decoding, its command line will contain the URL cache or encode and decode switches.

field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.
field_semantics.CommandLine: Full command line including arguments as supplied to the process.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Low; concentrated on certificate infrastructure hosts.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches come from certificate automation accounts on a small number of hosts. Tune with the invoking account and the certificate file path, and keep the URL cache option unfiltered.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the specific certificate automation service account on the enrolment servers only. Do not exclude the decode option globally, since it is the primary payload staging path for this utility.
test_strategy: Positive cases exercise the transfer option and the decode option. Negative cases keep the utility on ordinary store operations and use another binary with a similar switch.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1140.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
